records.issue_text: Webhook secret header lookup is case-sensitive on the header name while Node lowercases incoming headers, and comparison is not constant-time
records.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the secret check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Node/Next.js, incoming header keys are normalized to lowercase, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is configured with any uppercase characters (e.g. `X-Webhook-Secret`), this lookup will fail due to case-sensitive object key access. Additionally, the secret comparison is a plain `!==`, not a constant-time comparison, which is a verifiable security weakness in this diff for se
records.stripped_text: Webhook secret header lookup is case-sensitive on the header name while Node lowercases incoming headers, and comparison is not constant-time

records.issue_text: findFirst-then-create race in app-credential webhook can create duplicate credentials; needs unique constraint on (userId, appId) + upsert
records.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then branches to `prisma.credential.create(...)` if none is found. This check-then-act pattern is not atomic; concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe no row and both attempt `create`, which can lead to duplicate credentials unless a DB-level unique constraint exists. The diff does not show a unique constraint or an `upsert`/transaction to prevent this.
records.stripped_text: findFirst-then-create race in app-credential webhook can create duplicate credentials; needs unique constraint on (userId, appId) + upsert

That command generates 24 random bytes (then base64-encodes them), which contradicts the documented 32-byte requirement and can lead to misconfiguration/broken decryption when `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` is used.
